subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Lamborghini Countach
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Lamborghini Countach.

hook.text: The Countach was the poster car of the 1980s—literally on more bedroom walls than any other vehicle.

buildup.text: Marcello Gandini designed its sharp wedge shape with scissor doors that opened upward like wings.

discovery.text: The name comes from a Piedmontese exclamation—roughly 'wow!' said upon seeing something stunning.

twist.text: The rear visibility was so bad that drivers had to open the door and lean out to reverse.

climax.text: It was impractical, unreliable, and incredibly uncomfortable. Nobody cared—it looked like a dream.

punchline.text: The Countach sold on looks alone—and that was enough.

quiz.question: What does 'Countach' roughly translate to?
options: An exclamation of surprise or wow

details.summary: The Lamborghini Countach, produced from 1974 to 1990, defined the supercar with its radical wedge shape, scissor doors, and massive rear wing, becoming the quintessential bedroom wall poster car.
details.whyItMatters: The Countach established the visual language of supercars that persists today. No car before or since has so perfectly captured the fantasy of speed and excess in a single design.
takeaways: Designed by Marcello Gandini at Bertone in 1971
Scissor doors became a Lamborghini trademark starting here
Its V12 engine and dramatic styling made it an icon of the 1980s

faq.question: What does Countach mean?
faq.answer: It is a Piedmontese exclamation of astonishment, roughly equivalent to wow. According to legend, a worker at Bertone exclaimed it upon seeing the design for the first time, and the name stuck.

faq.question: Was the Countach actually fast or just flashy?
faq.answer: It was genuinely fast for its era, with a top speed near 180 mph. However, its driving experience was famously challenging, with poor rearward visibility, heavy controls, and a boiling hot cabin.
